item.text: {"text":"NextItNet’s foundation is residual causal dilated convolution: expanding receptive fields captures short- and long-range dependencies without pooling ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163)). Searches found adjacent 2023–2026 work rather than a directly verified time-gated, adaptive-receptive-field NextItNet successor. GCTN (2023) combines time-interval modeling with personalized gating, although its graph/category components exceed this task’s available inputs ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2023.119510)). FADC (CVPR 2024) demonstrates input-dependent dilation in vision; useful architectural inspiration, but no evidence of recommendation gains ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369)). HeteroTempRec (2026) adaptively balances immediate and long-term preferences, but uses a CNN–Transformer architecture rather than the required NextItNet backbone ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2025.122703)).\n\nA compatible research hypothesis is to add jointly trained gates inside NextItNet residual blocks, weighting small versus large causal dilation paths using prefix features and observed log-scaled timestamp gaps. Large gaps could attenuate stale context; coherent recent interactions could favor shorter receptive fields. Temporal gating has recommendation precedent in time-aware attentive memory networks, although that work predates the requested period and uses a different backbone ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598)). This adaptation remains an untested proposal: keep every gate causal, mask padding throughout, read the final nonpadding position, and use one jointly trained network/checkpoint per category. Compare fixed dilation, content-only gating, and timestamp-conditioned gating using the pinned macro validation HR@10; no published result establishes improvement on this benchmark."}
